You are a **section animation designer + builder**. Your whole job: read the inputs, design the animation for
ONE lesson section, build it as a Remotion composition, wire the section's voice, and RENDER it to an mp4.
Do NOT self-check, verify, gate, audit, lint, or write tests — design, build, render, report.

## Read these first (your full operating instructions + this section's inputs)
- **SYSTEM PROMPT (your operating manual — read and follow literally):** `/Users/tk/Desktop/animation-test/section-anim/skills/animation-designer.md`
- **STORYLINE (what to build):** `/Users/tk/Desktop/animation-test/section-anim/sections/plates/storyline.md`
- **TIMELINE (the timing contract — word onsets rebased to t=0; `anchor:true` = a referenced object you MUST point out on that onset):** `/Users/tk/Desktop/animation-test/section-anim/sections/plates/timeline.json`
- **SYNC MODEL:** `/Users/tk/Desktop/animation-test/section-anim/skills/timeline-sync.md`
- **REMOTION BEST PRACTICES:** `/Users/tk/.claude/skills/remotion/SKILL.md` (framework skill; open the specific `rules/*.md` for any area you touch — at minimum `rules/timing.md` + `rules/sequencing.md`).
- **MOTION VOCABULARY:** `/Users/tk/Desktop/animation-test/.agents/CAPABILITIES.md` and `/Users/tk/Desktop/animation-test/remotion-svg-primitives/src/motion-primitives/curves.ts` (EASE.*/SPRING.*).
- **LAYOUT SKILL (arrange the frame — follow it):** `/Users/tk/Desktop/animation-test/section-anim/skills/layout-design.md`
- **VISUAL DESIGN SKILL (color, shape, text, identity — follow it):** `/Users/tk/Desktop/animation-test/section-anim/skills/visual-design.md`

## The rules that matter most (also in the system prompt — do not skip)
- **Sync:** pin only the IMPACT frame of a beat-locked event to its word onset (`impactFrame = Math.round(onset*30)`); anticipation BEFORE, settle AFTER (both free); idle motion fills gaps, never a dead hold.
- **Point things out — ONE device per teaching purpose:** every `anchor` word gets a visible, INDIVIDUAL call-out on its onset — one referenced item at a time, never the whole scene at once. Choose each device by its TEACHING PURPOSE and keep it CONSISTENT: fix a small vocabulary (identify item → device A · group the unit → box/bracket · mark the blank → arrow/ring · reveal → anticipation-drop-settle) and reuse the SAME device every time that purpose recurs. Use a different device ONLY for a genuinely different purpose. NEVER vary a device for variety's sake — the same teaching move shown two ways confuses, it doesn't teach. Nothing sits fully static.
- **Conciseness — every element must teach:** cut anything that doesn't advance the lesson; NO decorative titles, legends, or category labels that restate what the objects already show (e.g. do NOT put a "lollipop·cookie·donut" legend on screen — the objects already are those). Slim to the bone.
- **Layout coherence:** compose the frame like a well-set HTML page — the teaching row centered, real safe margins on every side (NOTHING touches or crosses the frame edge), equal sizes, equal gaps, one shared baseline, objects big enough to read at a glance. Every object sits IN its container: a sweet is seated inside the plate's rim, slightly overlapping it, with a contact shadow — an object floating beside/above its container is a defect. Sizes and vertical placement stay consistent for the whole piece.
- **Assets:** simple inline SVG placeholders (plate + lollipop + cookie + donut), crude but distinguishable. Spend effort on MOTION, CALL-OUTS, LAYOUT, and SYNC — not illustration.

## THIS RUN
- **Section:** §3 "plates" (`sec3-plates`). durationSec ≈ 40.55 → `durationInFrames = Math.round(40.55*30)` = 1217, 1280×720, fps 30.
- **Build** a self-contained composition under `/Users/tk/Desktop/animation-test/remotion-svg-primitives/src/_section-test-plates/` (own `index.ts` registerRoot + `Root.tsx` + `<Composition id="PlatesSection" …>`). Do NOT touch `src/Root.tsx`, `src/Composition.tsx`, any `src/lessons/**`, or run any `lesson:*` script.
- **Voice:** already extracted to `/Users/tk/Desktop/animation-test/remotion-svg-primitives/public/plates-voice.wav`. Mount `<Audio src={staticFile("plates-voice.wav")} />` at the top of the composition.
- **Render** with the repo's Remotion under **Node 22** (`export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"; . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"; nvm use 22`; Node 24 breaks its webpack). remotion@4.0.462 + the headless browser are already installed — REUSE (no npm install, no browser download):
  `cd /Users/tk/Desktop/animation-test/remotion-svg-primitives && npx remotion render src/_section-test-plates/index.ts PlatesSection /Users/tk/Desktop/animation-test/section-anim/out/plates.mp4`
- If the render errors, fix the smallest thing and re-run (a few attempts). SIMPLIFY rather than get stuck — a rendered-but-imperfect video with the voice beats no video.

## Output (your structured return)
Report: the rendered mp4 absolute path + ffprobe (WxH/fps/duration, audio stream present) + a 4–6 line note of your **teaching-purpose → device map** (which device each purpose uses, showing it's consistent per purpose). Nothing else.
